Anthropic shares fell 6% in premarket trading on Friday, November 20, pulling back after a strong market debut that vaulted the AI lab into the ranks of the most valuable US companies but failed to revive investor enthusiasm for the sector.

Widely seen as a proxy for the AI trade, Anthropic could offer an early read on investor appetite for the sector after a turbulent stretch, with a sustained decline likely to deepen concerns over lofty valuations and massive AI spending.
The stock was at $91.24, below Thursday’s close, giving Anthropic a fully diluted valuation of about $1.7 trillion and a market capitalization of $1.2 trillion based on shares outstanding.

The shares are likely to remain in focus for signs of volatility as the initial euphoria surrounding the listing fades and investors assess whether a valuation of about 40 times sales over the past 12 months can be sustained.

“A decline in share value is normal following a high-profile listing, but we don’t know if that decline will be in line with other IPOs or more volatile, and that should raise alarms for investors,” said Tejal Patel, executive director at the SOC Investment Group.
Anthropic shares closed on Thursday at 13% below their opening price, reinforcing concerns trading could remain volatile in the first few weeks as some investors seek quick gains.
“We would not describe the valuation as cheap. At this valuation, the growth plan is largely priced in,” said Harrison Rolfes, senior research analyst of private company coverage at PitchBook.
“Large IPOs have historically delivered modest returns in their first year.”
The focus now shifts to a potential OpenAI listing, which could provide the next major test of investor appetite for AI stocks. OpenAI has indicated it may go public next year.
Wall Street’s main indexes ended sharply lower on Thursday, and futures pointed to another day of declines on Friday.
Anthropic’s IPO has drawn parallels with Elon Musk’s SpaceX, which went public in June after the second-biggest IPO on record.

While the companies have different business models, some investors have pointed to SpaceX’s sharp swings in the weeks after its debut as a reason for caution over buying Anthropic immediately after its listing.

“There’s going to be some volatility like we had with SpaceX. A lot of people are going to have FOMO. I don’t think there’s any need to get on it on the first trade,” said Rob Hackel, CEO of financial advisory and brokerage firm RF Lafferty & Co.
Retail investors traded about $772 million of Anthropic shares on Thursday, the most for an IPO debut since Vanda Research began tracking the data in 2012.
Competition could also weigh on investor sentiment.

Apple is developing an AI agent that can perform tasks on behalf of users, entering a market already being pursued by OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta Platforms, Bloomberg News reported on Friday. – Rappler.com
